title: New Method Pulls Faint Planets Out of Webb Images
paragraphs: Astronomers have a new way to find planets in pictures from the James Webb Space Telescope. The problem is that a bright star can hide a faint planet next to it. The star's glare is much stronger than the light of the planet.

The new method is called FLIP. Scientists built a digital copy of Webb's NIRCam camera. The copy shows many tiny problems in the camera, so the computer can guess the star's glare and subtract it from the picture.
In tests on known planets, FLIP found them two to 15 times better than usual methods. A team led by Caltech published the work in the journal Nature on 4 November 2026.

questions.q: What is the new method called?
What did scientists build on a computer?
questions.a: A digital copy of Webb's NIRCam camera.
